text:
zoe: Heads-up from this morning's Acme call: they want a trade-in + marketplace credit program for customers who upgrade hardware and commit to a 12mo marketplace spend. They want the field to be able to present it as a single offer. Thoughts?

paul-sales: Love the simplicity for customers. Key asks from sales: (1) show effective price after trade-in + credit, (2) clear renewal language so sellers don't overpromise.

ravi-partner-eng: Technically doable. Two implementation choices: attach trade-in rebate as a one-time private-offer line item or as a marketplace credit bucket consumed over time. Each has tradeoffs re: billing reconciliation.

ida-pricing: Prefer credit bucket consumed over time — aligns incentives. But we need expiry rules and a floor so net effective discount >= 10% after marketplace fees and device rebate.

nicole-legal: Legal requirements: proof-of-trade-in (serials + certified refurb vendor), anti-fraud checks, cap per-account, and clawback if evidence falsified within 12 months. Also want to avoid language that implies automatic renewal of credits.

acme-ops: Acme can provide serial verification feed and a shipment manifest. They prefer rebate as per-device fixed USD applied at checkout. They worry about marketplace latency on credit application.

paul-sales: If checkout application is slow we lose conversion. Sales strongly prefers immediate visible credit at checkout.

ravi-partner-eng: To support checkout application we need SKU wiring + marketplace entitlements + partner auth to accept serial feed. Rough estimate: 3 sprints for platform changes + 1 for partner integration. Canary NA -> EU.

ida-pricing: If partner pays gross credit (customer sees full discount) we need a partner settlement record. Ops must reconcile partner co-fund vs our discount ledger monthly.

marco-marketing: Messaging ask: do not publish exact $ trade-in amounts. Use ranges and focus on upgrade benefit + TCO reduction. Also want two case studies for launch: one SMB, one mid-market. Need assets 3 weeks before announcement.

paul-sales: Renewal scenario: if customer uses credits and then signs an annual contract, credits should not be double-counted. Sales suggests applying remaining credit to the first invoice of the new contract but not extending validity.

nicole-legal: Agreed. Draft clause: "Remaining trade-in credits may be applied to the first invoice of a new contract at Redwood's discretion; credits do not extend contract term or create new entitlements."

ida-pricing: Expiry proposal: 9 months for trade-in credits, 6 months for marketplace promo credits. Combined offers should default to the shorter expiry.

acme-ops: Request: allow mid-quarter top-ups for fast-moving deals. We'll support an API to push additional co-fund dollars.

ravi-partner-eng: API support ok, but we need idempotency and rate limits. Also need partner dashboard for reconciliation (aggregate numbers, not per-customer PII without NDA).

paul-sales: Training: create a 1-pager + 2 slide deck for sellers describing commit thresholds, example math, and FAQs about refund/clawback.

marco-marketing: I'll draft teaser copy and request two customer quotes from Acme's field.

nicole-legal: Also require a dispute resolution flow: partner has 60 days to raise reconciliation disputes; after that amounts are final.

ida-pricing: Ops questions: do trade-in rebates reduce our committed capacity targets for Dedicated customers? We should not let rebates be counted as committed revenue. Need a clear accounting note.

paul-sales: Sales ops: absolutely, rebates are not revenue. CPQ must show gross list price, rebate lines, and net revenue recognized separately.

ravi-partner-eng: Implementation note: extend private-offer schema with rebate_lines [sku_id, amount_usd, evidence_type, expiry_days] and a marketplace_credit object {amount_usd, expiry_days, apply_at: [checkout|postbill]}. We'll RFC this week.

acme-ops: We'll provide sample CSV of serials and agree SLA of 7 business days for verification.

zoe: Summary actions: (1) pricing ops (ida) to finalize expiry & floor by Wed; (2) partner-eng (ravi) to RFC schema and estimate dev sprints; (3) legal (nicole) to draft trade-in appendix + dispute clause; (4) marketing (marco) to draft launch plan & assets timeline; (5) sales (paul) to prep play 1-pager. Sync next Tue 10am PT.

sync-bot: Meeting created: "Trade-in + Marketplace credit launch sync" Tue 10:00 PT, 30m. Invite sent to participants. :white_check_mark:
